[agent-bulk] CORRECTED VERDICT -- I first recorded this event as over-clustered (likely) and then re-recorded it as vertex-bad after measuring the geometry; the earlier label is superseded, and the reason is worth reading because it is the trap. The star is NOT at a convergence: it sits in the middle of ONE straight through-going track ~375 cm long. Take the direction of the 232.4 cm grey pdg-13 segment 18036 near the vertex as an axis (it is unowned and it runs the +0 to +227 cm side). Ten of shower 18034's fourteen members lie on the SAME line on the other side: 18001, 29008, 51017, 52018, 53019, 56031, 57032 and the seed all sit 0.5-1.2 cm perpendicular of that axis, spread from s = 0 to s = -148 cm, and 29008 (34.3 cm, 58 fitted points, pdg 13) is antiparallel to the muon direction to 179.5 deg at 0.7-0.8 cm perpendicular. The muon's own scatter about its axis is 0.85 cm, so the far side is as straight as the near side: no kink at the star, no apex, one line. It is visible in ov-xz.png as a single horizontal streak crossing the whole event with the star in the middle of it, and it is what the az+065 vertex frame shows once you stop reading the star as a junction. Only 4 of the 14 members are genuinely off the line -- 50015/50016 (5.6 cm perp at s = -18 to -21) and 54020/55021 (20.5 cm perp at s = -104 to -120) -- which is the size and placement of delta rays or small EM blobs along a track, not of a 183 MeV shower. So the reconstruction has split one through-going track into a 232 cm muon on one side and a 183 MeV pdg-11 shower on the other, and no clustering judgement about 18034 is meaningful until the vertex is settled: this is a vertex result, not a clustering result. The reading I cannot exclude, and why this is likely and not certain: I have no dQ/dx across the star, so I cannot prove the two sides are one particle rather than two collinear ones; but 179.5 deg with sub-cm alignment over 148 cm is not something two independent particles do. This is the pilot's evt175896 pattern (a straight line through the vertex called two objects), sharper because here one side is already reconstructed as a 232 cm muon. Judged from the --vtx-span 60 close-in sweep as well as the native 262 cm framing; the close-in sweep is what first made it look like a clean muon-in/shower-out vertex, so the close framing alone was not enough on this event -- the whole-event ov-xz view and the axis measurement are what settled it. The OUT mark on 29008 stands and is stronger under this reading than under the old one: it is the backward continuation of the track. Showers NOT looked at: the 5 the scope rule skipped (46010 4.9 MeV, 48012 4.4, 49013 1.8, 45009 1.0, 47011 0.8), all under the 20 MeV threshold. No pi0 group and no second EM shower above 20 MeV.

No pi0: the reco made no group, and my hand pairing of the only two showers above 100 MeV (79074 + 13012) gives theta 104-106 deg and m = 291-294 MeV on both conventions, so I did NOT store it -- these two are not a pi0. [agent-bulk] shw 14007 (144.2 MeV, 5 seg, pdg 11, mcp2k nuecc): correct by the rubric, but UNCLEAR, and the reason is a knife-edge on the pass-1 angle cut that is the most reportable thing on this event. Vertex is good, judged from the native framing (99.7 cm half-span): the star is a clean three-prong junction -- 14001 (24.9 cm, pdg 2212) going one way and correctly left UNOWNED, 14007 going another, 14005 (63.4 MeV) a third, all three starting on it. 14007 is a proper shower: a broad continuous point cloud fanning from the X over ~24 cm, members covering it, single apex, no gap. THE DOUBT: on the acceptance plot the three cluster-48 segments 48038, 48040, 48041 sit as blue circles at 42.3, 43.2 and 43.8 cm and 25.4-26.3 deg -- just ABOVE the 25 deg dashed step -- while the member square 43021 sits at 39.0 cm / 24.9 deg, just BELOW it. So a 41.0 MeV three-segment object (28 pct of the shower energy) is rejected by 0.4-1.3 degrees at the same distance where a 0.1 cm stub was accepted by pass3_cone, and 37015 (0.4 cm, at 54.9 cm / 19.7 deg, metric 15.08) was accepted with a metric identical to 48038's 15.08. The reconstruction's own acceptance is therefore taking a 0.1 cm stub and leaving a 41 MeV cluster at effectively the same place. WHY I STILL RECORDED correct: the brief's under-clustering test asks for charge CONTIGUOUS with the member set, and cluster 48 is not -- in both the az-055 and az+085 shower frames it is a separate blob with its own point cloud, ~18 cm past the far end of 14007's body across visible empty space, and 26 deg is wide for bremsstrahlung off a 144 MeV shower. It is also not grey: it is shower 48040's own 3 segments, so correction 11's caveat applies and I did not treat 'owned by a neighbour' as evidence. TWO READINGS I could not separate, which is what unclear means here: (a) cluster 48 is the detached tail of this electron shower and the 25 deg cut lost it -- under-clustered; (b) cluster 48 is a separate small EM object correctly kept apart. NO IN MARK, deliberately: marking it would settle a question I did not settle. FALSE PI0 WARNING for whoever reads the pi0 block on this event: pairing 14007 with 14005 prices out at m = 140.2 MeV on the axis convention and the display labels it 'in the code's accept window', which is very close to 135 and tempting -- but their reco starts are (-97.0, 53.9, 68.2) and (-96.5, 53.7, 68.8), 0.9 cm apart and both ON the neutrino vertex, so neither can be a converted photon and this is a coincidence, not a pi0. The vertex convention correctly returns no mass (no chord from a gamma sitting on the vertex). The reco made no pi0 group and I did not store this pairing. Second shower, not the verdict: 14005 (63.4 MeV) is a 94-deg prong also off the vertex; in a nuecc event only one of 14007/14005 can be the electron, so one of them is a hadronic or photon prong carrying a pdg-11 label -- a PID question I am not deciding. Clustering statement, silent on PID. Showers NOT looked at: 47031 is in scope (74.9 MeV, 1 seg, 4.7 cm, pdg 2212, detached at 73-77 cm) and I only glanced at it; the 9 the scope rule skipped are 36014 (6.7 MeV) and 8 more all under 3.8 MeV.

[agent-bulk] shw 92061 (133.0 MeV, 12 seg, pdg 11, mcp2k other_em): correct. Vertex judged from the native framing (75.4 cm half-span, no re-frame needed): the star sits at the bend of the unowned cluster-17 pair 17001 (9.9 cm) + 17002 (19.4 cm), one prong leaving each way, and both are correctly left UNOWNED by every shower. 92061 is detached from it and made almost entirely of small fragments absorbed by pass4_angle (0.3 to 11.8 cm each, clusters 75-92), which looks alarming until you check the non-members: the acceptance plot for this shower carries NO unclaimed circle at all anywhere in 0-88 cm / 0-31 deg, i.e. every candidate inside the plotted window is already a member, and all 12 members sit inside the pass-1 dashed box (max 23.8 deg at 17.5 cm, and the farthest, 79034 at 67.4 cm, is at only 6.5 deg). So nothing contiguous is missing and nothing sits outside the gate. THE EVENT'S REAL QUESTION IS THE PI0, and it is a two-convention trap worth the owner's eye. There is no reco pi0 group (all pio_id -1) although the event has exactly two EM showers over 90 MeV, 92061 (133.0) and 89037 (97.6), both detached, with reco starts 12 cm apart. I assigned the slots by hand and stored the pairing: Epi0 230.6 MeV, asym 0.15, and then the conventions split -- axis convention theta 74.4 deg gives m = 137.8 MeV, which is 2 MeV off the pi0 mass and would be the best hand pi0 candidate in my shard, while the vertex convention theta 38.2 deg gives m = 74.5 MeV. The display flags both as inside the code's accept window; they cannot both be right. WHY I DO NOT TRUST THE 137.8: on pio-az-055-el+020 the direction from the star to gamma2's start and gamma2's own axis visibly disagree -- the start lies almost straight left of the vertex while the axis dives left-and-down -- and 89037 is a 19.6 cm object fitted from nine sub-2 cm fragments, so its axis is the weak measurement in the pair. The 38.2 deg vertex angle is built from the two START points and is the one I would trust more, and it does not give a pi0. Two starts 12 cm apart at 13-20 cm from the vertex ARE geometrically consistent with a pi0 of ~74 deg opening angle whose gammas each converted after about one radiation length, so I am not dismissing it either -- that is why it is stored as a candidate rather than asserted. This is a concrete instance of the pr/114 6.1 convention inconsistency deciding whether an event has a pi0 or not. Second shower, not the verdict: 89037 (97.6 MeV, 9 seg, 19.6 cm) is likewise a pass4_angle assembly of small fragments; its two nearby non-members 73028 (44.1 cm / 37.2 deg) and 77032 (47.7 cm / 33.2 deg) are 0.4-0.7 cm stubs well outside the cone, so it too has nothing obvious missing. Clustering statement, silent on PID. Showers NOT looked at: 56011 is in scope but is a 1.4 cm pdg-2212 stub (24.6 MeV) and I only noted it; the 21 the scope rule skipped top out at 7.4 MeV (50005) and the rest are under 5 MeV.

[agent-bulk] THIS IS A PID VERDICT AND THE EVENT THEREFORE CARRIES NO CLUSTERING JUDGEMENT on shw 8032 -- do not read it downstream as 'nothing wrong with the clustering here'; the member set of 8032 is in fact fine, it is the object that is not a shower. shw 8032 (262.1 MeV, 6 seg, pdg 11, mcp2k numucc_em, half-span 70.9 cm so the native framing was enough). The vertex is good: a clean two-prong V, the unowned 59.7 cm pdg-13 segment 8001 leaving one way and 8032 the other, both starting on the star, plus the unowned 3.6 cm pdg-211 stub 8031 at the vertex. WHY NOT AN EM SHOWER: 8032 is a SINGLE 56.1 cm segment of 95 fitted points that stays a thin uniform-width MIP for its whole length in both the az-055 and az+085 views -- no widening, no fan, no sub-showers -- and then makes a hard ~90 deg kink at 52 cm where 8009 (5.0 cm) and 8010 (4.3 cm) branch off, with two more pdg-2212/13 stubs (51015, 56020) at 48-50 cm. A 262 MeV electron in liquid argon has X0 = 14 cm and must start widening within one or two radiation lengths; it does not run 52 cm at MIP width and it does not turn 90 degrees. A pion that scatters hadronically at the end of its range does exactly this, and the little cluster of proton-tagged stubs at the kink is what that looks like. The display's own arithmetic agrees: the same charge read as a TRACK gives 157.7 MeV, which is right for ~56 cm of minimum-ionising track (2.1 MeV/cm gives ~120 MeV plus the end deposit), whereas 262 MeV read as a shower is not consistent with the shape. Confidence likely and not certain because I have no dQ/dx profile along the track -- that is the measurement that would settle it, and it is the one thing the display does not give me. What the clustering does look like, stated for completeness but NOT the verdict: the member set covers the object and nothing is missing -- the acceptance plot carries five member squares and no unclaimed circle anywhere in 0-68 cm / 0-26 deg -- so if the owner overrules the PID call, the clustering reading of 8032 would be correct. Second shower, checked lightly and NOT the verdict: 69027 (90.6 MeV, 7 seg, 21.4 cm) is a genuinely shower-like detached blob 36-47 cm from the vertex with a diffuse cloud, assembled from cluster 69 plus four pass4_angle fragments out to 53 cm; I saw nothing wrong with it but did not scan it segment by segment. No pi0: the reco made no group, and pairing 8032 with 69027 is meaningless because 8032 is not a photon -- note the vertex convention correctly returns no mass at all (8032 starts ON the vertex, so there is no chord), while the axis convention still prints 77.2 MeV and calls it in-window, which is a good example of that convention accepting a pair the geometry forbids. Nothing stored. Showers NOT looked at: the 2 the scope rule skipped, 49013 (5.8 MeV) and 50014 (3.2 MeV).

[agent-bulk] shw 85085 (101.7 MeV, 4 seg, pdg 11, mcp2k other_em): under-clustered, and it is the clean grey-charge case rather than the ambiguous owned-by-a-neighbour one. Vertex judged from the --vtx-span 60 close-in sweep (the native framing is 320.6 cm half-span because of the long tracks and is useless for this): the star is a genuine multi-prong convergence and I have no complaint about it. 85085 is a detached blob 24-39 cm from the vertex. THE MISSING PIECE: 85058, 14.0 cm long, 24 fitted points, pdg 11, in CLUSTER 85 -- the same cluster as every one of the shower's four members -- sitting 8.5 cm from the shower start at 27.2 deg with metric 0.64, and its owner field is '-', i.e. NO shower claims it. It is grey, so correction 11's first-owner-wins trap does not apply here. In both the az-055 and az+085 shower frames it runs along the lower edge of the very same point cloud the members sit in, contiguous with them, not across a gap. On the acceptance plot it is the circle at (8.5 cm, 27.3 deg), just above the 25 deg dashed step. Four of cluster 85's five segments are members and this is the fifth. Marked IN. A SECOND FINDING ON THE SAME SHOWER, and it probably explains the first: START/AXIS WRONG. The orange axis arrow points down and to the right, away from the member body, and the acceptance plot proves it numerically -- two of the three plotted members sit at 40.7 and 62.5 deg FROM THEIR OWN SHOWER'S AXIS (85062 and 85061, both pulled in by from_vertices walk_add rather than by the cone). An axis that its own members miss by 40-62 degrees is not measuring this object, and the pass-1 angle gate is being applied around it, which is a plausible mechanism for rejecting 85058 at a nominal 27 deg while accepting members at 62. I record under-clustered because that is the closest available verdict string; the phrase start/axis wrong is written here so these events can be grepped and counted (correction 9). Confidence likely rather than certain because 85058's 14 cm could in principle be a separate short track laid across the blob rather than shower charge, and I cannot separate those from shape alone at this size. Two more circles on the acc plot, NOT marked and much weaker: 75048 (0.4 cm) at 22.7 cm / 40.8 deg and 74047 (0.3 cm) at 34.9 cm / 35.7 deg, both owned by 91075 and both sub-centimetre -- if the owner reverses anything here, reverse those, not 85058. Showers NOT looked at in any detail: this is a 35-shower, 62-segment event and the scope rule reached 8 -- 15018 (222.6 MeV but pdg 2212), 23030 (97.7), 89069 (97.4, pdg 2212), 22024 (92.4, pdg 13), 87065 (59.7), 88068 (35.9), 15011 (25.9). I judged only 85085, the leading pdg-11 object; the other 27 showers are all under 11 MeV. This verdict is a claim about ONE shower, not about the event. No reco pi0 group; I did not price a pairing because the two leading objects by charge are proton- and muon-tagged and the pdg-11 showers are spread over four candidates with no obvious pair. Clustering statement, silent on PID.

[agent-bulk] shw 10051 (120.4 MeV kine_charge / 72.4 kine_best, 1 seg, pdg 11, mcp2k nuecc): under-clustered, and the mechanism is SPLITTING rather than a missed neighbour. This event is ONE broad EM shower -- a single continuous point cloud fanning out of the neutrino vertex over ~40 cm, the textbook nuecc electron, and the star sits exactly at its apex, so the vertex is good (native framing, 51.4 cm half-span, no re-frame needed). The reconstruction threads that one cloud with SEVEN overlapping polylines all starting on the vertex, and turns four of them into four separate showers: 10051 (21.3 cm), 10052 (23.5 cm), 10054 (29.1 cm) and 10056 (24.8 cm), plus three left unowned -- 10050 (17.6 cm, pdg 211), 10057 (29.6 cm, pdg 13) and 10012 (4.0 cm, pdg 2212). Every one of them is in cluster 10 and every one reads dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 against every other, which is the display's degenerate readout for exactly this situation. It is visible in one frame: in shw10051-az-055-el+20 and again from 140 deg away in shw10051-az+085-el+20, the yellow member halo covers only the short blue strand near the apex while orange, green, red, grey and purple strands run through the SAME cloud beside it. So the verdict shower holds roughly one seventh of an object it should hold all of. Marked IN: 10052, 10054, 10056 -- the three cluster-10 strands that are other showers' seeds. Two caveats on those marks, stated because they matter for how the mark is read. (1) I marked only the three SEEDS, not the cluster-36/37/38 fragments those showers also own (36038, 37039, 38041 under 10054; 38042, 38043 under 10052), because those live in the detached blob 33-41 cm out beyond a visible gap and whether that blob belongs is a separate question I did not settle. (2) I did NOT mark the unowned strands 10050 and 10057 even though they run through the same charge, because they carry pdg 211 and 13 tags, i.e. the reconstruction is holding them as track hypotheses, and marking them would be a PID statement dressed up as a clustering one. If the summed shower energies here are ever used as a total, note that four showers threading one cloud is a double-counting hazard: 120.4 + 106.3 + 75.5 + 23.9 = 326 MeV of kine_charge assigned to a single ~40 cm nuecc shower. I did not verify how the code shares charge between overlapping segments, so treat that as a flag to check, not as a measurement.
